name: Ops Dash Connector
author: Legacy Sales Engineering
changelog: 1.9.1 - Audit accuracy behind bot protection: new read-only page-signals endpoint lets Ops Dash verify a page's index state (noindex), SEO title/description and content stats straight from WordPress when a CDN bot challenge (e.g. Cloudflare) blocks the dashboard's crawler. Fixes pages being wrongly flagged as 'set to noindex' on protected sites. No settings, no behavior changes on the site itself. 1.9.0 - Post categories: Ops Dash can now list this site's categories, create new ones, and publish posts into the right category (find-or-create by name at publish time). Posts published without a category continue to use the site default. 1.8.2 — Pairing endpoint updated: Ops Dash moved to its own server, so the one-time site-pairing exchange now points at the new address. Nothing changes for sites that are already connected — they keep their stored connection key and continue to receive pushes exactly as before; this only affects connecting a brand-new site. No other code changes. 1.8.1 — Packaging fix: the 1.8.0 archive was built on Windows with backslash paths, so on Linux WordPress hosts it extracted without a proper plugin folder — the plugin could not be found and would deactivate itself. The zip is now a correct POSIX archive (opsdash-connector/). No code changes from 1.8.0. 1.8.0 — Full metadata push on publish: the focus keyword is now written to Rank Math / Yoast / AIOSEO (posts get an SEO score instead of showing as having no SEO data); sites with no SEO plugin now get Open Graph + Twitter share tags and a self-referencing canonical from the connector's own head output. 1.7.3 — update checks: a manual Check Again on Dashboard → Updates now sees new releases immediately (manifest cache busted on forced checks; routine cache 1h). 1.7.2 — llms.txt endpoint: Ops Dash can publish/refresh an llms.txt (AI-assistant site summary) as a physical file at the web root, with one-time backup of any pre-existing file. 1.7.1 — robots.txt fixes now work even when a physical robots.txt exists at the web root: the original file is backed up once and the managed rules are written into it; resetting to the WordPress default restores the backup. Clear warnings when the file is not writable. 1.7.0 — One-code pairing: connect a site by typing an 8-character code from Ops Dash instead of copying the long key; the plugin exchanges the code for the key automatically. Manual key entry moved to Advanced. 1.6.x — packaging + self-heal fixes, self-updating, robots.txt-sitemap-heading fixes.
